artifact.scope: Teaching comparison frame for the supplied bench-clamp concepts. Both requirements remain proposed with unknown hardness. Criteria are conservatively treated as hard gates pending clarification; no performance scoring, recommendation, test execution or engineering validation is established.

conditions.text: ProblemBrief revision r1 supplies proposed REQ01 retention and REQ02 damage prevention. Both have unknown hardness and undefined acceptance limits.

M01 is a provisional teaching datum because its supplied description connects screw closing and reverse-screw release. This choice implies no customer preference, approval or demonstrated feasibility.
Customer loads, workpiece properties, geometry, damage criteria, available actuation resources and applicable safety constraints remain unknown.
The supplied lunar-sampling excerpt has unestablished transferability and provides no basis for clamp performance judgments.

M03 retains its upstream conditional exclusion: its assumed pneumatic topology lacks the screw transmission required by its release option. This is a conceptual inconsistency, not a measured retention or damage failure.

criteria.text: Gate pending hardness resolution: retain the intended workpiece throughout the intended operation under conditions and allowable movement yet to be established. Include unresolved support reactions, disturbance and input-loss behavior in later review; no separate approved safety requirement exists.
Gate pending hardness resolution: engagement, holding and release must meet a damage criterion yet to be agreed. Material, finish, geometry, contact effects and inspection method remain unresolved.

judgments.basis: The supplied screw route hypothesizes position retention after input stops. Transmission geometry, friction, disturbances, support conditions and required loads are undefined. Datum status does not establish gate passage.
The proposed contact-distribution option and reverse-screw release have no supplied damage assessment. Workpiece properties, contact conditions and acceptable changes are unknown.

The supplied pneumatic route assumes sustained supply and coordinated return behavior. Supply availability, leakage, input-loss response, load conditions and support reactions are unresolved. No relative advantage over M01 or gate passage can be established.

The shared contact-management hypothesis does not establish equal damage performance. Pneumatic closing and elastic return introduce undefined contact and release conditions; neither acceptance limits nor comparative evidence is supplied.

sensitivity: An eventual holding load, duration and allowable movement could change the assessment of screw position retention and sustained pneumatic restraint; no ordering is currently supported.
Material, finish and damage limits could change acceptable contact conditions for either route. Shared contact-distribution language cannot justify a same judgment.

Supply availability and required input-loss behavior could constrain M02; operator capabilities and release clearance could constrain M01. These are unresolved use conditions, not confirmed customer preferences.
Changing the datum to M02 would leave all current gate judgments unknown. Counting symbols or assigning weights would not resolve the missing acceptance criteria or evidence.
unknowns: Who can confirm REQ01 and REQ02, their hardness and acceptance criteria? Recommendations remain empty until unknown hardness is resolved.
What work operation, loads, directions, durations, workpiece properties and allowable movements define retention?
What constitutes damage during engagement, holding and release, and how will condition be assessed?
What applicable safety requirements, operator constraints and bench interfaces must be established? No additional requirement IDs or approved safety gates are invented here.
Is manual input or pneumatic supply available and acceptable, and what response is required after input loss, slip or incomplete release?

After use conditions are defined, plan comparable retention and before-and-after condition assessments for M01 and M02 using agreed workpieces, loads and limits. No procedure execution, measurements or acceptance results are supplied.
M03 requires a revised release mechanism or explicitly revised topology before reconsideration. Its conditional exclusion establishes no performance ranking among M01 and M02.
